title: Signed gift reports that a later filing replaced, against the published list of gifts
question: When a department files a second report for the same month, what happens to the gifts on the first one in the public list of gifts?
finding: The published list carries none of the 52 signed filings that a later filing replaced (0 envelopes appear in it). On 42 of them, 494 gifts worth $2.9 million in 34 department-months appear on no filing the list holds; in 10 the filing the list carries repeats the gifts. The largest losses: Recreation and Parks (REC), May 2026 $750,055; Recreation and Parks (REC), November 2024 $565,000; Recreation and Parks (REC), August 2026 $338,944; Recreation and Parks (REC), February 2026 $338,337. 4 gifts worth $393,750 that an amendment removed are itemised under a later month of the same department and are not counted as lost. This confirms with the signed PDFs what the site’s “Gifts to departments” page inferred from the cover pages: the list keeps only the last filing of each month, and an amendment that adds a late gift erases the original's donors from public view.
how: Each signed PDF is read for its type, department, month, total and every gift (donor, date, value, the four yes/no answers and the contract text); spreadsheet uploads are read from the printed table. A gift is "in the list" when a gift of the same donor (letters and digits only) and value is itemised under the same filing series in the list downloaded 12 November 2026. The "filing the list carries" is the cover-page row whose envelope the list holds.
limits: The printed upload tables wrap names over two lines and 2 uploads were read short of their stated count (168 of 180, 98 of 123); a gift whose donor was retyped differently in the amendment counts as missing. Amending a report to add a late gift is what the form provides for; the fault is in how the dataset is published, not in the filings.
